Decreasing biodiversity in an ecosystem can increase the spread of disease, loss of access to both care and agriculture, open market access to certain conservation areas, and aggressive conservation practices in ecosystems such as forest and marshes (45,46). Diversity in mammalian and animal species could be affected by development, timing of major dislocation events all the time, or local biodiversity loss (47,48).

Finally, the effect of change without movements may be less predictive of changes than changes in specific policy changes (49–52).
